name: Google Drive (vault sync)
purpose: Reads the live Watch Tower vault (Markdown) from the Drive folder instead of the bundled snapshot.

envVars.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
envVars.description: OAuth 2.0 client ID (Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials).

envVars.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
envVars.description: OAuth 2.0 client secret for that client.

envVars.name: GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN
envVars.description: Refresh token for Junior's Google account, granted the read-only scopes listed below.

envVars.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_VAULT_FOLDER_ID
envVars.description: Drive folder id of the vault. Defaults to 1CHIRqiewFlQF4JvzPgxXJDRSV2L-lXdl.

setupSteps: In Google Cloud Console, create (or reuse) a project and enable the Google Drive API, Google Calendar API and Gmail API.
Configure the OAuth consent screen (External, Testing is fine) and add Junior's Google account as a test user.
Create an OAuth client ID of type 'Web application'. Add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorised redirect URI.

In the OAuth 2.0 Playground (gear icon > 'Use your own OAuth credentials'), authorise these read-only scopes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata — then exchange the code for a refresh token.
In the FastAPI backend environment, set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN (Preview and/or Production), then restart the backend.
Optional: set GOOGLE_DRIVE_VAULT_FOLDER_ID if the vault folder moves.

name: Notion (reading log)
purpose: Reads Junior's reading log (a database or page) for the Morning Brief. The page is still to be identified (see the blocked task).

envVars.name: NOTION_TOKEN
envVars.description: Internal integration secret (Notion > Settings > Connections > Develop or manage integrations).

envVars.name: NOTION_READING_LOG_ID
envVars.description: ID of the reading log database or page (the 32-char id in its URL).

setupSteps: Go to https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations and create an internal integration with 'Read content' capability only.
Copy the integration secret into NOTION_TOKEN.
Open the reading log in Notion, choose ••• > Connections > add the integration, so it can read that page/database.
Copy the 32-character id from the reading log URL into NOTION_READING_LOG_ID.
Set both in the FastAPI backend environment and restart it.

name: Slack (Cosmos AI workspace)
purpose: Confirms the bot can see the Cosmos AI workspace and, optionally, shows the latest messages from one channel.

envVars.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
envVars.description: Bot User OAuth token (xoxb-…) of a Slack app installed in the Cosmos AI workspace.

envVars.name: SLACK_CHANNEL_ID
envVars.description: Optional channel id (C…) to show recent messages from. Needs channels:history and the bot invited to the channel.

setupSteps: Create a Slack app at https://api.slack.com/apps (From scratch) in the Cosmos AI workspace.
Under OAuth & Permissions add read-only bot scopes: team:read, channels:read, and (optional) channels:history.
Install the app to the workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token into SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.
Optional: invite the bot to a channel (/invite @yourapp) and set SLACK_CHANNEL_ID.
Set these variables in the FastAPI backend environment and restart it.

name: Obsidian (vault Markdown)
purpose: The vault itself is the source of truth. Read from the live Google Drive folder when Drive is connected, otherwise from the snapshot bundled at build time.

envVars.name: VAULT_SOURCE_DIR
envVars.description: Optional local vault source for npm run snapshot. The backend uses its bundled snapshot when live Drive is unavailable.

setupSteps: Nothing to configure for the bundled snapshot: it is refreshed every time `npm run snapshot` runs on a machine that has the vault at ../watchtower (or VAULT_SOURCE_DIR).
To read the live vault instead, connect Google Drive (see above). The app then reads the Drive folder on each request (cached for 60 seconds).
Open the same folder in Obsidian via Google Drive for desktop to edit it (see the vault README).
